answer: Each identity runs inside a hardware enclave and signs its work with a key bound to that enclave. A failed audit slashes the bond behind the key, and the quote proves the key cannot be cloned onto a second machine. Ten clones on one host produce one quote, so the quill of duplicate accounts collapses at the first check. No identity may audit its own recruit, which keeps a velvet surface of look-alike accounts from grading each other. At dawn the bond is all that stands between an operator and a wipeout.
